system_gain.note: [feeds g(gain); model.g_at interpolates it log-linearly]  moved unchanged from ptc_constants.json.  rule 3 of protocols/02-ptc.md: the slope of pair-difference variance against signal, weighted 1/var^2, with the intercept fixed at session 01's R^2 (L10).  Mean over the four CFA planes; per-plane values are in ptc_gain.csv and spread 2.02% at worst.  Uncertainty is the scatter of the fitted rungs, not a formal error

pedestal_fit.note: [feeds the pedestal in the star-colour constraint]  moved unchanged from bias_constants.json.  pedestal = A + B * 10**(gain/200), fitted per conversion-gain branch, split at gain 200; uncertainty is the worst residual (L27)

hcg_threshold_gain.note: [selects the branch of pedestal_fit]  moved unchanged from bias_constants.json.  lowest gain of the high-conversion-gain branch; the fine grid steps by 2, which is the uncertainty.  ZWO's own published curve annotates 200 (vendor/asi585specs/) and the retired project measured 200 -- one prediction, not two, and this reproduces it.  The 'ZWO say 252' belief has no source; 252 is the ASI2600's threshold (L26)

t_dead.note: [feeds N = T_night / (t + t_dead)]  moved unchanged from sky_constants.json.  rule 4: the mean frame-to-frame DATE-OBS gap minus exposure, in steady state, over 144 intervals.  A MEAN and never a median -- the median is 32.00 s here and the model consumes the mean, so a median would understate the overhead.  Measured under this night's dither cadence, which was every frame; the archive dithered every second frame and measured 17-20 s

F_sky.note: [feeds F_sky, per CFA plane]  moved unchanged from sky_constants.json.  rule 3 of protocols/06-sky-pair.md: the modal level of the sky ROI, pedestal subtracted, x g(gain), per frame, averaged over the night.  Sky ROI is the bottom-right corner, 512x512 at (3264, 1584, 512, 512), chosen once as the darkest of the four corners and then never moved.  An UPPER BOUND on true sky: unresolved nebulosity is inside the box and cannot be separated -- and it is the right bound for the model, which needs the level sitting under the faint signal.  The uncertainty is the pedestal's alone, at one count, because no bias bracket was shot on the night and the pedestal comes from notebook 15's bench block at the same setpoint and gain

dark_current_bound.note: [feeds D, at the fixed -10 C setpoint]  moved unchanged from dark_constants.json.  an upper bound, not a value, and never a signed one (L14).  The implied rate read off each exposure separately spans -2.004e-02 to +1.009e-03 e-/px/s and disagrees in sign, which is what a dark current cannot do.  What limits it is the offset state, not statistics: the state step over a 600 s exposure is 8.49e-04 e-/px/s, while the statistical floor is 1.3e-6.  L14 inherited < 1e-2

eta_comb.unit: measured sd reduction against the ideal sqrt(N)
eta_comb.note: [feeds eta_comb; model.eta_at interpolates it in log N]  moved unchanged from dark_constants.json.  measured on the BIAS stack, not the dark stack.  L15 required frames that need no registration; darks satisfy that and then stall on their own DSNU, which is a property of darks and not of combination.  Bias carries no dark-signal non-uniformity (session 01's bias_fixed_pattern_ratio 1.011), so it isolates the rejection-and-averaging half honestly.  Averaging is ideal to N~8 and then approaches a fixed-pattern floor of 0.2426 counts.  This is an upper bound on the real loss: no registration, no resampling, and the sky half is unmeasured

linear_to_at_least.note: [feeds ceiling(gain) in the star-colour constraint -- the proved-straight bound, never the clip]  moved unchanged from linearity_constants.json.  the highest level this ladder proved straight: the mean over the four CFA planes of the last rung with under 1% of its pixels at the top code, in the central 256 box.  A LOWER BOUND on the linear range and not an edge -- above it the pixels are pinned and this ladder has nothing to say, not because the sensor was shown to bend there.  Its resolution is one rung, 4% of t_sat, and no interpolation can improve on that because there is no crossing to interpolate towards.  Uncertainty is the per-plane scatter.  Per-plane values are in linear_to_per_plane; every rung is in linearity_rungs.csv

linear_to_at_ladder_gain.note: [feeds ceiling(gain) at the validation gain]  NOT MEASURED.  The linearity ladder ran at gains ['50', '100', '200'] and the NGC 7000 validation ladder was shot at gain 252.  Deliberately not interpolated: linear_to_at_least is the last rung a ladder PROVED straight, at a resolution of one rung, and a value between two gains would be a guarantee no frame supports.  Fixed by a short linearity block at gain 252; nothing else in the model waits on it

system_gain_restated_move_pct.unit: percent change from session 02's published system_gain
system_gain_restated_move_pct.note: [not consumed by the model]  how far session 04's restated g sits from the PTC table published above, per gain.  Carried so the size of an open record decision is visible in the file the model reads, without being a second table anything could eat by accident.  See state_repair_constants.json for the restated values themselves

read_noise_counts.note: [feeds R(gain); model.read_noise_e multiplies it by g at the point of use]  assembled by 23_model_constants.ipynb from bias_sweep.csv, which 03_bias_sweep.ipynb wrote -- the provenance is that notebook's, not the assembler's.  Pair-difference sigma over root two, mean over the four CFA planes, at offset 15 and -10 C.  62 gains from 0 to 450, in tens with a grid of twos through the HCG threshold.  Stops at 450 per the gain-domain rule in CLAUDE.md; session 01's rows above it remain in bias_sweep.csv.  Uncertainty is the per-gain standard error
